must_build: Every page in ui-spec/gcp/networking.json (16 pages; nav: VPC networks, IP addresses, Internal ranges, Bring your own IP, Firewall, Routes, VPC connectivity, Shared VPC, Serverless VPC access, Packet mirroring, VPC Flow Logs)
Backend: VPC network: networks, subnets, firewall rules, routes via the existing gcp compute/network handling (grep core/ providers/)
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/gcp/networking.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass

Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: VPC network peering
limitations: networks.addPeering / removePeering are real: a peering is ACTIVE only once both networks peer, subnet routes are exchanged (non-transitive) and Connectivity Tests route across it. Custom-route import/export flags are stored but not applied; offline packet enforcement across peered networks is compiled but not covered by the real-packet test.

depth_targets.title: Private service connection
limitations: Allocating ranges for Google-managed services and the private-services-access connection to them is not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Network firewall policies (hierarchical / regional policy resources)
limitations: Vyomi models the classic per-network VPC firewall rule, not the newer Network Firewall Policy resource (its own rule evaluation order and org/folder attachment).

depth_targets.title: VPC Flow Logs (Subnets / VLAN attachments / Cloud VPN tunnels)
limitations: No VPC Flow Logs export. Offline with netsim enforcement on, real per-flow counters exist and core/netsim/flowlogs.py renders GCP flow records from them, but nothing writes them to Cloud Logging yet.

depth_targets.title: Internal ranges
limitations: The Internal Range Allocator (planning/reserving CIDR blocks across an org before they're assigned to subnets) is not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Bring your own IP (BYOIP)
limitations: Advertising customer-owned IP ranges over Google's network requires real BGP/RPKI infrastructure Vyomi does not have.

depth_targets.title: VPC connectivity (Cloud Interconnect, Cloud VPN, Network Connectivity Center)
limitations: Hybrid connectivity to on-premises or other clouds needs real tunnels/circuits; Vyomi's network model stops at the project boundary.

depth_targets.title: Shared VPC (host/service project attachment)
limitations: Vyomi's Compute core is single-project; cross-project host/service VPC sharing and its IAM delegation are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Serverless VPC Access connectors
limitations: Connectors bridge serverless products (Cloud Run/Functions) into a VPC; Vyomi does not run a serverless data plane that would use one.

depth_targets.title: Packet mirroring
limitations: Mirroring clones live packets to a collector; Vyomi has no data plane producing real packets to mirror.

depth_targets.title: Cloud Router + Cloud NAT (regions/*/routers)
limitations: Routers and their NAT configs are real resources (insert/get/list/patch/delete); a NAT covering a subnet gives its external-IP-less VMs internet egress in Connectivity Tests and, offline with enforcement on, real masquerade. BGP sessions, NAT IP allocation/ports and logging are not modeled.

Offline, the rules are enforced on REAL packets (one Docker bridge per subnet + an nftables table per space, core/netsim/enforce.py) only when VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1|auto and the instance runs on the Docker compute backend; with enforcement off (the default) or on LXD/Multipass runtimes they are evaluated, not enforced.

note: SINGLE GOAL FOR THIS RUN (orchestrator): build the GCP 'Network Intelligence Center > Connectivity Tests' console screens (list, create test form: source/destination instance or IP, protocol, port; detail page with the reachability result and the hop-by-hop trace, rerun, delete) on the EXISTING native networkmanagement v1 API (core: projects/{p}/locations/global/connectivityTests — already served on Nano and offline from core/netsim reach()). Add it to the networking nav like the real console, a capability entry gcp.networking.connectivity-tests (already full — keep it true), a UI<->wire smoke round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-gcp.mjs (create via UI -> GET over wire shows the result; create over wire -> shown in UI), and a live fixture.
